result.answer: No. The message's intent was to place the patient in WARD-B, bay BAY2-04, as of 09:20 UTC. That placement has since been overtaken. The PAS later sent a transfer to WARD-C, bay BAY1-07, with event time 09:45 UTC. The bed-management system behind Downstream Out applied it, and its record now shows the patient in WARD-C. That system has no receipt for the WARD-B transfer, so it never got it. If the receiving system only needs the current placement, then the WARD-B transfer adds nothing. Resending it would move the patient back to a ward they have already left. Your 'what if' is in fact how this receiver is set up today: it keeps the current state only. That is why Shutter closed the case with nothing sent. I agree with that plan. The one thing lost is the record of the stop in WARD-B. That only matters if the site wants a full movement history. In that case the alternative applies: cancel the WARD-C transfer, resend both in order, and hand the case to a person (W1). That setting is not in place now. From this case alone, Shutter cannot tell whether anyone downstream needs the WARD-B stay.
